`readfiscalnz` is intentionally strict at each boundary: release selection,
transport, artifact validation, parsing, semantic validation, caching, and
series replay. An error is preferable to silently changing an accounting
regime or accepting an unverified workbook. This article shows how to locate
the failing stage, recover safely, and collect maintainer-useful diagnostics
without exposing credentials.

The examples below use a packaged synthetic CSV and a temporary cache. They
are deterministic and offline.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(readfiscalnz)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)

fixture <- system.file("extdata", "hfi.csv", package = "readfiscalnz")
if (!nzchar(fixture)) {
  stop("The installed hfi.csv fixture is unavailable.")
}

cache <- tempfile("readfiscalnz-troubleshooting-")
dir.create(cache, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

error_text <- function(expr) {
  tryCatch(
    force(expr),
    error = function(condition) conditionMessage(condition)
  )
}
```

## Locate the failing stage

| Stage | Typical symptoms | First checks |
|---|---|---|
| Release selection | unknown family or `release_id` | `list_nz_fiscal_releases()` and exact identifier |
| Terms and transport | `accept_terms` refusal, timeout, HTTP or redirect error | review `nz_fiscal_terms()`, use a local file, check bounded timeout |
| Artifact validation | unsupported extension, empty/oversized file, missing XLSX/CSV signature | confirm the path, extension, file size, and source bytes |
| Official integrity | catalogue SHA-256 mismatch | retain the artifact and report release ID plus hashes; do not bypass the check |
| Parse and schema | missing sheet, canonical column mismatch, changed labels | use the correct family reader and inspect the release structure |
| Semantic validation | accounting, date, unit, consolidation, or forecast-status drift | treat as upstream/schema change; do not coerce values silently |
| Cache/provenance | missing or corrupt raw snapshot | rerun the reader from the original local file or official release |
| Series replay | invalid or absent 64-hex identity, duplicate dates | obtain `series_id` directly from `nz_fiscal_series_catalogue()` |

## Capture a safe error message

For a reproducible report, capture the condition message while keeping the
original input and cache private. The helper below returns only that message.

```{r safe-errors}
missing <- file.path(tempdir(), "readfiscalnz-no-such-file.csv")
missing_message <- error_text(
  read_nz_hfi(file = missing, cache_dir = cache)
)
missing_message
```

The local-file error means the reader did not start parsing. Check
`file.exists(path)`, `tools::file_ext(path)`, and the path's read permission;
do not work around it by downloading an arbitrary similarly named file.

If no local file is supplied, terms refusal occurs before network transport.
This is the expected offline failure, not evidence that a cached parser result
was lost.

```{r terms-error}
terms_message <- error_text(
  read_nz_hfi(
    release_id = "hfi-1972-2025",
    cache_dir = cache,
    accept_terms = FALSE
  )
)
terms_message
```

To use the live path, inspect `nz_fiscal_terms("hfi-1972-2025")`, then set
`accept_terms = TRUE` explicitly. If the goal is an offline build or test,
pass a saved local artifact instead. A local artifact avoids live network
access and the live terms gate, but the package still attaches its pinned
catalogue terms metadata and the source terms remain applicable.

## Recover from schema and semantic failures

Readers accept only `.xlsx` workbooks or canonical `.csv` files with the exact
family schema. A file with the wrong columns should fail before producing a
partially interpreted result.

```{r schema-error}
bad_csv <- tempfile("readfiscalnz-bad-", fileext = ".csv")
writeLines(c("wrong,columns", "1,2"), bad_csv)
bad_message <- error_text(
  read_nz_tax_outturn(file = bad_csv, cache_dir = cache)
)
unlink(bad_csv)
bad_message
```

Do not fix a schema error by renaming or reordering columns until the source
layout has been reviewed. The supported release, parser version, and schema
version are part of the package contract. An upstream Treasury layout change
requires a catalogue/parser update and new tests.

For a genuine local replay, start with a fresh cache and the original saved
artifact:

```{r valid-replay}
valid <- read_nz_hfi(
  release_id = "hfi-1972-2025",
  file = fixture,
  sheets = "Spending",
  cache_dir = cache
)
stopifnot(inherits(valid, "nz_fiscal_data"))
```

If this succeeds but an official read fails, compare the release ID and
expected catalogue hash, then retain the non-secret HTTP status or error text
separately. When provenance is available, inspect `resolved_url`,
`retrieved_at`, and `raw_sha256`. Do not replace a failed official hash check
with a fixture unless the fixture route is explicitly the analysis being
tested.

## Repair a missing or corrupt cache entry

The raw snapshot is content-addressed and verified by
`nz_fiscal_raw_bytes()`. Removing a temporary snapshot makes the failure mode
explicit; rerunning the reader from the original local file rebuilds it.

```{r cache-repair}
snapshot <- nz_fiscal_provenance(valid)$raw_snapshot_path
stopifnot(file.exists(snapshot))
unlink(snapshot)

missing_snapshot_message <- error_text(nz_fiscal_raw_bytes(valid))
sub(
  snapshot,
  "<raw-snapshot>",
  missing_snapshot_message,
  fixed = TRUE
)

repaired <- read_nz_hfi(
  release_id = "hfi-1972-2025",
  file = fixture,
  sheets = "Spending",
  cache_dir = cache
)
stopifnot(
  identical(nrow(repaired), nrow(valid)),
  file.exists(nz_fiscal_provenance(repaired)$raw_snapshot_path)
)
```

`nz_fiscal_raw_bytes()` never downloads a replacement. If the original local
file is unavailable, recover it from the analysis archive or rerun the
catalogued official route after reviewing terms. `prune_nz_fiscal_cache()` can
remove old raw snapshots, so preserve an in-use path during maintenance.

## Diagnose series-history errors

Series identities are lowercase 64-character SHA-256 strings returned by
`nz_fiscal_series_catalogue()`. They are not display names and should not be
typed by hand.

```{r series-error}
invalid_id_message <- error_text(
  nz_fiscal_series_history(valid, "Core Crown expenses")
)
invalid_id_message

series_catalogue <- nz_fiscal_series_catalogue(valid)
stopifnot(nrow(series_catalogue) > 0L)
history <- nz_fiscal_series_history(
  valid,
  series_catalogue$series_id[[1L]]
)
stopifnot(inherits(history, "nz_fiscal_data"))
```

If a valid identity is absent, confirm that the same release, surface, and
parser options were used to build the catalogue. A changed accounting basis,
unit, or actual/forecast role intentionally creates a different identity.

## Maintainer validation without secrets

When emailing chartwellmacro@gmail.com, include the package version, R version, operating
system, release ID, reader arguments (with local paths shortened), and the
selected provenance fields. Include `raw_sha256` and `catalogue_sha256`, but
do not include private file paths, credentials, cookies, or full environment
dumps.

```{r maintainer-diagnostics}
safe_provenance <- nz_fiscal_provenance(valid)
safe_provenance[c(
  "provider", "family", "release_id", "source_kind", "raw_size_bytes",
  "raw_sha256", "catalogue_sha256", "parser_version", "schema_version"
)]
```

For a local checkout, the maintainer validation sequence is:

1. Run the offline package tests with `testthat::test_local()` and confirm
   that the packaged fixtures reproduce their expected schemas and values.
2. Build a source tarball and run `R CMD check --as-cran` in a clean library.
3. For an official-source issue only, run the package's explicit live
   validation with the required environment and terms decision; retain the
   available `resolved_url`, `retrieved_at`, and artifact hash, and capture any
   non-secret HTTP status or error details separately. Never retain credentials.

The live path is deliberately opt-in. A normal check, vignette build, or
package load must not depend on Treasury availability. If a failure repeats
with the same release and clean local fixture, report the safe diagnostics and
the smallest reproducible input so the parser can be updated deliberately.

```{r cleanup, include=FALSE}
unlink(cache, recursive = TRUE)
```
